prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Technetium (테크네튬) itself — the sovereign of the Technetium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a clear, innocent purity; olive skin; oval face; medium-sized eyes — narrow upturned eyes, level outer eye corners; soft rounded brows; upturned nose; full heart-shaped lips; steel-blue eyes; a bare, makeup-free face.
Body and hair: lean and toned — a slim, firm waist with softly defined vertical abs and lightly sculpted arms and shoulders, a full bust build; a short tousled pixie cut with choppy uneven bangs; smooth satin silver-grey hair with a machined lustre and a cool cyclotron-violet sheen in the shadows.
Expression: one brow slightly raised, attentive eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: technetium: a silvery-grey metal and the first element made by human hands, found in 1937 in a strip of molybdenum sent across the ocean from a cyclotron and later named from the Greek word for artificial; the lightest element with no stable isotope, so almost none survives on Earth; for decades the gap below manganese held only mistaken claims, yet in 1952 its lines were seen in the light of red giant stars, proof that stars forge elements; today it is the most used medical tracer, lighting up bones and hearts.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Tarnished-silver and workshop-cream armor with large symmetrical wing binders behind her built from precise machined plates like a hand-made instrument, each plate etched with fine spectral lines and edged in cyclotron violet-blue light, a small red-giant ember core at the chest, light body armor; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: large wing-shaped binder plates spread symmetrically behind her back as the main shape, with light body armor. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: tarnished silver grey, cyclotron violet-blue, red-giant ember red, clean workshop cream.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a research station orbiting a swollen red giant star: an observation deck facing the vast red star, a spectrum hall where its light is spread across the walls as a rainbow band crossed by the dark lines of the elements it forges, white corridors washed in red starlight.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Tc) and atomic number (43) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
